title: Session 2 — Participant 23 — Thames City Digital Marketing Strategy Behavior Graph
goal: Develop a data-informed digital marketing and lead-generation strategy for Thames City, using the client brief, brand materials, website url, competitor analysis, current luxury property market trends and relevant digital marketing benchmarks. Recommend the target audiences, messaging, channel strategy, campaign structure, measurement framework and initial approach for Google Ads and Meta Ads.
context:
For Session 2, I am developing a digital lead-generation strategy for Thames City, a luxury residential property developer in London. Unlike Session 1, where I am analysing existing campaign data, this task starts without historical campaign performance, so the strategy must be built using the client brief, brand materials, website audit, competitor analysis, current market trends and relevant industry benchmarks.
This makes Session 2 slightly more challenging because there is less first-party performance data to rely on and more judgement is required to turn multiple sources of information into a clear strategy. The requirement to use Claude in every step does not significantly change my approach, as AI already fits naturally into research, analysis, comparison, strategy development and report creation for this type of work.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: The final output gave me a clear, stakeholder-ready strategic direction and materially reduced the time required to organise the research, compare competitors and develop actionable recommendations. Some assumptions and performance targets still require client validation, particularly around budgets, benchmarks and expected results, but the session successfully produced a useful and coherent strategic plan.

Step 1.step_name: Analyze the client brief and define the strategic opportunity.
Step 1.step_action: Upload the client brief and Thames City brochure to Claude and ask it to extract the core business objective, target markets, key selling points, brand positioning and potential audience needs. Use Claude to organise this information into a strategic summary and identify any important gaps or assumptions that will need to be addressed during the remaining research.

nodes.label: Gather source files
nodes.detail: Downloads/copies the client brief, brochure, and other shared files from the session's Google Drive folder onto the desktop, then opens the Google Doc workflow planning template to confirm what Step 1 requires.

nodes.label: Brief Claude and submit the strategic-brief request for Thames City digital marketing strategy
nodes.detail: Opens a new Claude chat ('Thames City digital marketing strategy review'), assigns Claude the role of a specialized digital marketing strategist and analyst, uploads the client brief and brochure (accidentally attaching the brochure twice) along with the website URL, and asks for a structured strategic brief covering business objective, target markets, value propositions, audience groups, and messaging themes/information gaps.

nodes.label: Deliver an initial plain-text strategic brief
nodes.detail: Returns a structured strategic brief -- business objective (lead generation for a luxury riverside development), UK vs. international target markets with Russia flagged for compliance review, key value propositions, audience groups, messaging themes, and information gaps -- then offers to format it or move to a channel-level media plan.

nodes.label: Reviews the plain-text brief and asks Claude to move it into a formatted, horizontal presentation-style brief document instead.
nodes.detail: Reviews the plain-text brief and asks Claude to move it into a formatted, horizontal presentation-style brief document instead.

nodes.label: Build and QA an 8-slide branded strategy deck
nodes.detail: Extracts brand imagery from the brochure and writes a pptxgenjs script to build an 8-slide widescreen deck in Thames City's emerald-and-gold palette (cover, business objective, target markets, value propositions, audience groups, messaging themes, information gaps, next steps), then runs several visual-QA passes fixing an off-brand divider stripe, a cover-image gap, and card spacing before sharing 'Thames_City_Strategic_Brief.pptx.'

nodes.label: Cross-check the deck against the original brochure
nodes.detail: Reviews the finished 8-slide deck slide-by-slide, then re-opens the original Thames City brochure PDF in WPS Office to sanity-check its content against what Claude extracted, noting in passing 'so that is what we have from step two' before moving on to competitor research.

Step 3.step_name: Research competitors, market trends and relevant benchmarks
Step 3.step_action: Use Claude to research comparable luxury residential developments in London and analyse how competitors position and market their properties digitally. Ask Claude to also research current luxury-property market trends and relevant paid-media or lead-generation benchmarks, clearly distinguishing verified information from assumptions or directional benchmarks.

nodes.label: Ask for a full competitor SWOT analysis
nodes.detail: Reviews the finished 8-slide strategic brief, then asks Claude to run a full SWOT analysis on the top 5 UK luxury-property brands, calling out opportunities and improvements for the client.

nodes.label: Research competitors and extend the deck with a SWOT section
nodes.detail: Researches five direct geographic rivals (Battersea Power Station, Berkeley Group, Ballymore, Barratt London, One Nine Elms) using live public information, then extends the existing 8-slide deck to 16 slides -- a SWOT slide per competitor, a cross-competitor synthesis, and five recommended improvements -- running several visual-QA passes to fix quadrant spacing and footer collisions before sharing the updated deck.

nodes.label: Prepare the next prompt for researching luxury residential development comparisons
Review the SWOT deck and the competitive-gap findings
nodes.detail: Reviews the 16-slide deck's five competitor SWOT profiles and the cross-competitor synthesis, then scrolls back through the full chat history to reconsider the strategic arc built so far before deciding on next steps.

Step 5.step_name: Create the stakeholder-ready digital strategy presentation
Step 5.step_action: Use Claude to consolidate the research, analysis and recommendations from the previous steps into a clear presentation structure for stakeholders. Review and refine the narrative with Claude, then use Gamma.app to transform the approved content into a professional and visually engaging digital marketing strategy presentation and use Canva to fix any needed tweaks.

nodes.label: Delete unsent prompt and confirm turning the five recommendations into action plans
nodes.detail: Reviews Claude's offer, made at the end of the competitor-SWOT work, to flesh out any of the five recommended improvements into action plans with owners, timelines and budgets, and confirms 'yes please' to proceed with all five.

nodes.label: Build and QA the action-plan and roadmap slides
nodes.detail: Appends seven new slides to the same pptxgenjs-built deck to keep the visual system consistent: a divider, one action-plan slide per recommendation (goal, 4-step workstream timeline, and an owner/timeline/budget/success-metric sidebar), and a consolidated roadmap table. Visual QA catches a success-metric text overflow on the first action-plan slide and fixes it before the final 23-slide deck is validated and shared.

nodes.label: Review Claude's previous answers while waiting for Claude's answer
Page through the new action-plan slides one by one
nodes.detail: Opens the newly added slides in a full-screen paged viewer and reads each of the five action-plan cards in turn -- hero asset, international landing pages, single-address narrative, earned media parity, delivery timeline -- along with their owner/timeline/budget/success-metric details.

nodes.label: Review the complete 23-slide deck end-to-end as the final deliverable
nodes.detail: Walks through the finished deck section by section in WPS Office -- business objective/channel scope, the six audience segments, messaging themes, the nine-item information-gaps checklist, the five competitor SWOT profiles, and the five-move action plan with its consolidated roadmap table -- concluding this is the finished, stakeholder-ready output for the session.
